name: Initial contact (email)
description: Sent once, on the enquiry itself. Deliberately template-rendered rather than model-written: the first message a stranger receives should be the same message every time, and it is the one nobody wants a model improvising.
subject: Thanks for getting in touch

name: Initial contact (SMS)
description: Identifies the sender in the first clause. An unidentified SMS from an unknown number is both a bad first impression and a TCPA exposure.
content: {{sender.displayName}} here from {{tenant.name}} — thanks for your enquiry{{#if context.interest}} about {{context.interest}}{{/if}}. I'll be in touch shortly. Reply STOP to opt out.

name: Educational (email)
description: The middle of the sequence. Sends something useful and asks for nothing, which is what makes the later ask land.
subject: {{#if context.topic}}{{context.topic}}{{else}}Something that might help{{/if}}

name: Promotional (email)
description: The only template that carries an offer. Every field of the offer arrives in the event payload — the engine has no promotions table and does not want one (§0.5 Seam D, D12).
subject: {{context.offerName}}

name: Re-engagement (email)
description: The last message in the sequence, and it says so. A nurture sequence that never admits it is over is the thing that gets a sender marked as spam.
subject: Still worth a conversation?
